punchline: Thich Nhat Hanh says anger is a howling baby, and what the baby needs is to be held.
thirty_sec: Thich Nhat Hanh compares anger to a crying baby that needs its mother to embrace it. In one passage a mother strikes her crying baby and fails to see that she and the child are one. When anger rises, you start mindful breathing at once and hold the anger while you breathe. You try not to say or do anything yet. Instead of shouting at your anger, you find out what it is crying for.
